q: Pseudorandom generators (PRGs) in complexity theory produce an n-bit string from a short seed s of length O(log n) such that no polynomial-time test can distinguish the output from truly random. The existence of PRGs is equivalent to:
exp: Håstad-Impagliazzo-Levin-Luby (1999): PRGs exist iff one-way functions exist. OWFs are functions easy to compute but hard to invert (for a random input). Their existence is implied by most cryptographic hardness assumptions (discrete log, factoring, etc.).
